title: SLA threshold to customer communications automation playbook
author: Maya Lin
body:
Summary
This playbook describes the automated flow that translates tenant-level SLA/SLO threshold crossings into standardized customer communications and escalations. It covers detection rules, decision logic, message templates, required signals and telemetry, automation wiring (PagerDuty, Slack, SES, webhook), and manual intervention checkpoints. The goal is to deliver timely, consistent, and context-rich notifications while minimizing noise and protecting customer trust.

When to use this playbook
- Any tenant or customer whose availability, latency, or quality SLOs cross pre-defined warning or critical thresholds.
- During prolonged degraded throughput, persistent model-quality regressions for a tenant, or when downstream rate limits impede production traffic.
- As the canonical source for automated customer-facing comms; do not create ad-hoc messages outside this flow unless authorized.

Ownership and stakeholders
- Owner: Customer Success - Tenant Reliability (customer-success)
- On-call liaison: Platform SRE (eng-sre)
- Automation owner: Integrations team (eng-platform)
- Legal & Privacy reviewer: Security & Compliance (security-and-compliance)
- Communications lead: Customer Success Comms (customer-success)

Required signals and telemetry
- SLO evaluations (per-tenant): 1m and 5m rolling windows from the SLO engine.
- Latency p95/p99 and error rate per route (from Redwood Console metrics API).
- Throughput and queue length (serving-runtime metrics).
- Model quality regressions: evaluation harness alerts tied to customer prompt-sets.
- Active incident state from Incident Manager / PagerDuty.

Threshold definitions (table described)
- Warning: 3 consecutive 1m windows where SLO_missing_rate >= 5% OR p99 latency degraded > 50% vs baseline for 10m.
- Actionable: sustained degradation for 30m (SLO_missing_rate >= 10% OR p95 latency > 2x baseline).
- Critical: 60m sustained OR customer-visible errors affecting >=5% of requests in last 5m.

Decision matrix (high-level)
1) Warning -> internal ticket + scripted silent notification to customer (low-urgency email) after verification window.
2) Actionable -> escalate to on-call, open customer-facing incident channel (dedicated Slack channel + email) and run mitigations.
3) Critical -> Incident declared, trigger high-priority PagerDuty, send immediate customer SMS/email if configured, and route to senior CS + engineering leadership.

Automation flow (end-to-end)
1. Detection: SLO engine emits event -> Telemetry Gatekeeper evaluates thresholds.
2. Dedup & enrichment: Gatekeeper enriches event with tenant metadata (contract tier, contact preferences, active rate limits, pinned model versions) via Customer Metadata Service.
3. Policy decision: Rules engine selects message template and channel per tenant policy. Logic considers: tier, private/dedicated deployment, contractual notification SLAs, and regulatory constraints.
4. Communication: Message dispatched via Communication Orchestrator which supports: email (SES), transactional SMS (Twilio), webhook to customer webhook endpoint, and creating a private Slack channel for the incident.
5. Escalation: If no acknowledgement within configured window, escalate via PagerDuty to on-call and then to manager chain per escalation ladder.
6. Close loop: When SLO returns above threshold and stays stable for configured cool-down window, send recovery notification and update customer incident record and QBR metrics.

Message templates (examples)
- Warning (email subject): [Redwood] Service performance advisory for tenant {{tenant_name}}
  Body: "We detected a temporary degradation in response times for your tenant between {{start}} and {{end}}. Our systems are monitoring and you may experience intermittent latency. This is informational; no action is required unless you observe functional impact. If you would like faster updates, reply with 'subscribe'."

- Actionable (email + Slack): [Redwood] Degraded availability for tenant {{tenant_name}} - engineers engaged
  Body: "We have observed sustained elevation in error rate affecting approximately {{percent}} of requests. Our on-call engineers are investigating. Temporary mitigation steps: fallback to lower-cost model variant, reduce request concurrency, or enable autoscale burst for Dedicated. Estimated next update: {{eta}}.
  Action items: (1) Confirm whether in-progress traffic is OK to route to fallback variant (yes/no). (2) Provide any recent schema or prompt-set changes that may impact behavior."

- Critical (SMS + Email + Slack): [Redwood] Immediate action: Production impact for tenant {{tenant_name}}
  Body: "We are experiencing production-level impact for your tenant. Our senior engineers are engaged and we will provide continuous updates in the private channel. If you have a hotfix or immediate traffic control you want us to apply, reply with the instruction and contract-signed operator will execute after verification."

Notification policy and cadence
- Warning: single informational mail, 60-minute follow-up if persists.
- Actionable: initial notice immediately, follow-ups every 30 minutes until mitigated, then hourly for the first 6 hours.
- Critical: immediate notice + follow-ups every 15 minutes for first 2 hours, then every 30 minutes.
- All messages must include: root cause hypothesis (if available), mitigation steps taken, ETA for next update, who is the point of contact, and a link to the private incident channel and ticket number.

Escalation ladder (ordered)
1. Customer Success On-call (first responder)
2. Platform SRE on-call (operational mitigations)
3. Serving Runtime Owner (model execution mitigations)
4. Integrations/Network (if related to private networking/DNS/firewall)
5. Customer Success Manager / Account Owner
6. Director, Customer Success / Head of Platform (executive notification)

Manual overrides and sensitive customers
- For restricted/high-profile customers (confidentiality: restricted), all automated messages must be routed through the CS Manager for approval before external dispatch. This is enforced by a flag in Customer Metadata Service.
- Manual override steps: Authorized CS manager may pause automation via the Communications Orchestrator UI. After a pause, manual messages must reference the incident ID and be logged in the incident record.

Operational runbook (step-by-step)
1. Verify: Confirm the telemetry event in Redwood Console and the SLO engine. Run the query: SELECT tenant_id, window_start, p99_latency, error_rate FROM slo_evals WHERE tenant_id='{{tenant_id}}' AND window_start >= now() - interval '60 minutes';
2. Triage: Determine whether degradation is model, infra, or customer input related. Check: recent model rollouts, quantization profile changes, and recent customer prompt-set uploads.
3. Mitigate: Apply one of the following (ordered by least user-visible):  a) Activate KV cache warmup for hot prefixes. b) Route to dedicated lower-latency pool if available. c) Enable autoscale burst for Dedicated tenant. d) Fallback to a verified older model variant.
4. Communicate: Use the Communication Orchestrator to dispatch the appropriate template and open the private channel. Attach logs, key metrics, and the mitigation steps.
5. Track: Update the incident ticket with every customer-facing message and record time to acknowledgement.
6. Recovery: When SLOs are restored for the cool-down window, send recovery and summary, and schedule a post-incident review.

Automation wiring examples
- Sample webhook payload (Communication Orchestrator -> Customer Webhook):
  {
    "incident_id": "INC-20260203-1234",
    "tenant_id": "tenant_987",
    "severity": "actionable",
    "summary": "Elevated error rate: 12%",
    "start_time": "2026-02-03T14:12:00Z",
    "links": ["https://console.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20260203-1234"]
  }

- PagerDuty trigger example (curl):
  curl -X POST https://events.pagerduty.com/v2/enqueue \\
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\
    -d '{"routing_key":"<pd_integration_key>","event_action":"trigger","payload":{"summary":"Tenant tenant_987 critical latency","severity":"critical","source":"redwood-slo-engine"}}'

Testing and verification
- Test scenarios must include: transient spike (warning), sustained degradation (actionable), and catastrophic outage (critical).
- Create synthetic tenants in staging and configure varying contact preferences (email-only, webhook-only, email+SMS).
- Verify the deduplication logic works when repeated SLO events are emitted in a short window.
- Unit tests: rules engine policy selection and channel mapping. Integration tests: Communications Orchestrator to SES/Twilio/webhook and PagerDuty.

Audit and compliance
- All outgoing communications are logged to the Incident Archive (retention default: 365 days).
- For restricted customers, messages routed through CS Manager must include the approval id and timestamp.
- Attach transcripts of private Slack channels and webhook delivery responses to the incident record for legal audits.

Post-incident actions and QBR inputs
- Owner must complete an incident summary within 72 hours and tag the incident with cause, mitigations applied, time-to-detect, time-to-ack, time-to-recover.
- Include incident metrics in the next QBR: token-level cost delta during incident, SLO impact window, customer-reported impact.
- If the incident crosses contractual SLA thresholds (credits owed), route to Finance + Legal with the incident packet.

Appendix: quick-check checklist (for responders)
- [ ] Confirm telemetry and tenant metadata
- [ ] Verify escalation ladder and contact availability
- [ ] Choose mitigation (cache/route/fallback) and apply
- [ ] Dispatch initial customer message via Orchestrator
- [ ] Open private channel and pin logs + metrics
- [ ] Document all messages and trigger post-incident summary

Contact directory (roles with sample contacts)
- Customer Success On-call: cs-oncall@redwood.ai
- Platform SRE: platform-oncall@redwood.ai
- Integrations owner: integrations@redwood.ai
- Legal: legal@redwood.ai
